extracted.intended_audience: Public Information Officers (PIOs), agency administrators, incident managers, family liaisons, and other agency personnel responsible for managing communications and administrative actions during serious injuries/fatalities and critical incidents (wildland fire and other emergencies).
extracted.subtask_description: Operational checklist and procedural guidance for Public Information Officers and agency leaders to prepare for, respond to, and follow up after critical incidents (including serious injuries and fatalities), focusing on notifications, family liaison, CISM, communications, administration, and investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare Delegation of Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a Delegation of Authority for the critical incident management team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The delegation can be edited at the time of the incident to reflect specific complexity and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain emergency notification information
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure ALL employees have current emergency notification information on file (secured yet accessible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update information as seasonals are hired; must have street addresses (no PO boxes); ensure information is easily accessible in an emergency (see Appendix A for form fields).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify family liaison(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify family liaison(s) for when serious injuries or fatalities occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select one family liaison per family but consider need for assistants; see Family Liaison, Appendix B, for selection, preparation, and communication guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop local emergency operating plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop local emergency operating plan which includes initial response and notification procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include critical incident communication procedures as part of this plan (see Information and Communications rubric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide training and conduct exercises focusing on interagency cooperation, coordination, and incident management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include simulation exercises for Public Information Officers and trainee assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure capable designated personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure key personnel designated to manage the critical incident are capable, organized, and clearly understand their roles and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate back-ups and clarify responsibilities in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop contact list for reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop contact list for reporting process (see Agency Reporting Log, Appendix C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify your agency’s process for reporting and investigating serious injury or deaths including procedures for reporting shelter deployments and entrapments.

rubrics_metrics.name: NICC notification for wildland fire fatalities
rubrics_metrics.description: For wildland fire fatalities, entrapments and burnovers, notify the National Interagency Coordination Center (208-387-5400) within 24 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NWCG Form PMS 405-1. Individual agency follow-up is still required by Agency Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: OSHA notification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure notification of Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) area office within eight hours for certain incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify within 8 hours for death of any employee from work-related incident, and for inpatient hospitalization of three or more employees as a result of a work-related incident (see Appendix D for external phone numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Next-of-kin notification process
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish process/protocol for notification of next of kin in case of serious injury or death; coordinate with local authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Fatality/Serious Injury Notification Guide (Appendix E); provide next-of-kin notification prior to release of victim names publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family liaison support resources and policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify resources available to assist designated family liaisons and internal policies that may apply when assisting the family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources: grief counselors, peer supporters, administrative support. Policies: autopsy for work-related death, death benefits coverage, procedures for processing personnel papers, advice for filing claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify CISM protocols and resources pre-incident
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that Critical Incident Stress Management (CISM) protocols and resources are identified prior to the occurrence of a critical incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify local/regional/area CISM resources (peer support, defusing, debriefing) and contact them to discuss activation/capabilities/costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify Employee Assistance Program (EAP) capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and its capabilities in grief counseling, family support, and critical incident stress support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate EAP contact information and roles in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop critical incident communication procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop critical incident communication procedures as part of a local emergency operating plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include agency jurisdictions, directory of support (local/regional/national), directory of agency experts (qualified PIOs, crisis comm teams, contract communicators), key spokespersons, list of communication tools/resources, process for setting up communication center, and coordination of information dissemination with accident investigation team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create fact sheets, bio-sketches and glossary
rubrics_metrics.description: Create fact sheets and bio-sketches for agency and community as well as a generic format for additional fact sheets and a glossary of terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare templates in advance to expedite information release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create media contact lists and graphics capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Create media contact lists including phone and fax numbers and identify technical expertise for producing maps and graphics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphics may include directions for family visits to fatality site or memorial service; maintain up-to-date media lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure PIO formal training and simulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure Public Information Officers receive appropriate formal training and participate in simulation exercises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include trainee assignments and exercises that simulate critical incident scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare administrative agreements and resource lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Create, review, update, and/or renegotiate MOUs/MOAs/BPAs/contracts and draft Delegation(s) of Authority to manage critical incidents; establish resource list of experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreements may support interactions with local law enforcement, medical facilities, counseling/CISM services, lodging; compile experts for personal/tort/workers’ comp/death benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish nearest medical/burn/trauma resource list
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a list of the nearest medical facilities, burn/trauma centers, hours of operation and transport capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep this list current and readily accessible (see Appendix D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic review of emergency notification info
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that emergency notification information is periodically reviewed and updated and easily accessible in an emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must include street addresses (no PO boxes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for casual hires and correct contact recording
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat casual hires/ADs/EFFs as agency employees and ensure their emergency contact information is recorded accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to NWCG IIBMH and ensure accurate emergency contact info on Fire Time Reports (OF-288).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference agency casualty and benefits guides
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference respective agency guides (e.g., employee casualty guide) that contain available benefits, how to file claims, and when SSA should be contacted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure administrators and family liaisons know these procedures and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarize with investigation laws, guidelines and cooperators
rubrics_metrics.description: Become familiar with laws/regulations for local/county/state/tribal jurisdictions and their roles for investigating critical incidents and review agency accident investigation guidelines/procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet and develop rapport with key local law enforcement administrators; conduct joint training and simulation exercises; participate in local emergency response/public safety council meetings regularly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Administrator roles during incident
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency Administrator should provide care for survivors/coworkers/families, determine scope/jurisdictions, request assistance, provide Delegation of Authority, determine management level using pre-identified ICS criteria, implement reporting/notification, identify key contacts, prepare for investigation and determine/implement CISM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participate personally when possible; be readily available to provide direction, guidance and support as needed; advise SAIT of CISM actions taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial action checklist (risk assessment and verification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct risk assessment on rescue/recovery operations and ensure rescue/recovery response is activated; gather and verify initial information (Who, When, What, Where).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement local emergency operating plan and communications procedures; control communications to guarantee privacy of names until next of kin are notified; obtain victims’ personal emergency notification information for notification; coordinate with home duty stations for off-unit employees; contact tribal leadership immediately for Native American victims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement notification and reporting during incident
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement agency notification procedures; do not release victims’ names prior to official notification to next of kin; coordinate with law enforcement/coroner/medical examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediately notify critical incident PIO when family/internal notification is complete so public release can proceed; initial agency press release will be made by designated PIO to preserve integrity of the notification process; state only facts and DO NOT SPECULATE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family liaison duties during incident
rubrics_metrics.description: Designate family liaison(s), consider unique circumstances, assign one person per family (allow resource assistance and the opportunity to decline), coordinate communications among liaisons, be available within first 24 hours, facilitate family attendance at agency-sponsored events, provide networking and access to EAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider appropriate representative(s) at hospitals, shuttle points; coordinate multiple liaisons via calls or meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activate and manage CISM during incident
rubrics_metrics.description: Activate CISM resources as needed and coordinate logistics, capacity, and participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HRSP may assist if IMT assigned; coordinate location away from incident/media, transportation, refreshments, lodging; ensure resources can handle magnitude (number of participants, mobilization timeframes); CISM generally implemented within 48–72 hours; initial CISM for directly involved personnel, relieve personnel from external responsibilities, keep crews together, hold separate sessions, and ensure confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement information & communications during incident
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement critical incident communication procedures including developing strategy, setting up communication center, hotlines/websites, internal bulletin boards, and ordering qualified incident information officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate lead PIO, confirm roles and responsibilities across local unit PIO, IMT PIO, cooperator IOs, incoming resources, and SAIT IOs; establish approval process and primary spokesperson; provide information to victim/family first; release fatality names only after next-of-kin notification; never release names of injured or missing; brief receptionists/dispatchers; document events and contacts and prepare maps/graphics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media engagement and messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Make immediate contact with local media, develop relationships, and be prepared to respond within minutes using prepared messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop initial prepared statement: show concern; say what is being done/how quickly agency responded; list resources that responded; give verified releasable facts; report current status; do not speculate; confirm the obvious; discuss initiation of investigation if appropriate; stress safety; mention environmental impacts if appropriate; thank cooperators; inform public what they can do to help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media access, logistics and protective measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide and coordinate media access to incident site in cooperation with IMT and SAIT; brief media on site/air restrictions; consider media pool arrangements and anticipate media needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate logistical needs (phones, work areas), photos/biographies, deadlines, protective gear, photo/video opportunities, and interviews; use newsletters and established tools; develop community liaison; protect rights of employees who do not want media contact; coordinate media access at funerals and memorials; prepare condolence letters within 24 hours; prepare for official visits and provide briefing materials/escorts/transportation/press conference logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document and archive incident events
rubrics_metrics.description: Document all events, contacts, and evidence throughout the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain chronology, contact log, photos, and designate a single source for administrative record keeping and tracking; designate a records person familiar with FOIA regulations and follow up with FOIA contact for archiving/dissemination after the incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative workload and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate local unit’s added workload and request assistance as needed; designate individuals to prepare/process necessary paperwork and to coordinate recovery of personal items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request experienced coaches, additional personnel to maintain daily operations, consider relief from work targets, designate record-keeping lead, designate fiscal representative for travel/funeral/transportation/funding questions, and assist SAIT as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation coordination and briefings
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure investigation teams receive thorough briefings about what happened, jurisdictions, current activities, personnel lists, key officials, cooperators, safety officers, and legal implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to host and cooperate with SAIT; clarify and agree upon roles, responsibilities, authorities and objectives; determine delegation sources and public information handling/spokesperson; coordinate forwarding of safety information (preliminary reports, safety alerts) through agency channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Administrator after-incident responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure key individuals (families, survivors) are briefed on the accident investigation report prior to its release, provide subject-matter experts to answer questions, debrief and release CISM providers, and monitor stress reactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for stress reactions during release of reports, anniversaries, and memorials; provide EAP and expedite administrative requirements (claims, benefits); conduct After-Action Review (AAR) to develop recommendations, update plans and share lessons learned; follow up on corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family liaison post-incident duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue working with family members on claims, information requests, site visits, obituary assistance, and funeral arrangements; provide debriefing/stress counseling for liaison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue regular communication but establish a mutually agreed conclusion to official involvement; provide family with follow-up resources and brief on potential future contacts (e.g., media attention on anniversaries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications transition and follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a communication transition plan to ensure ongoing dissemination of information regarding the critical incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address continuing impacts (staff rides, visitors, traffic, media, production companies), identify need for follow-up committee, requests for memorials, plan return visits to incident site, evaluate and adjust public information activities, and develop mechanisms to send follow-up information to families/survivors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-incident administration and benefits assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assist survivors and families with paperwork for workers’ compensation, death benefits, and other applicable benefits; provide process for filing tort claims if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain contact information for fiscal and contracting experts assigned during the incident; provide benefits packages to families so they are aware of entitlements (including DOJ Public Safety Officer’s Benefit where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation close-out
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure accident investigation team closes out with the Agency Administrator and appropriate agency officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm dissemination of final reports and implementation of recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency notification form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect comprehensive emergency notification information for employees, including primary and secondary next-of-kin details and medical wishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form fields include physical home addresses (no PO boxes), primary/secondary contacts, phone numbers, workplace contacts, known medical conditions, who should be notified, wishes regarding life support, blood type, organ donor status, clergy contact, people to not notify, and pet care details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting and preparing family liaisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations for selecting family liaisons: local preference, availability within first 24 hours, willingness for long-term commitment, pairing for backup, assessing pros/cons of a friend-of-family liaison, and personal attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select steady, level-headed individuals who listen well and can maintain objectivity; allow chosen liaisons the opportunity to decline; preparations include physical/mental/emotional readiness, appropriate attire, having another person accompany first visit, anticipating questions, keeping records, asking rather than assuming, using yes/no questions when decisions are required, meeting families at varied locations, coordinating with other liaisons, and scheduling regular check-ins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles for communicating with families
rubrics_metrics.description: Key principles: LISTEN and DO NOT ARGUE; avoid starting sentences with 'you'; reduce defensiveness by avoiding general statements and focusing on specific needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break complicated information into small pieces, do not assume it has been understood, assist families in setting achievable goals (funeral arrangements, benefits meetings), and set a final meeting to officially end the liaison assignment to avoid over-dependence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up contacts and benefit processing support
rubrics_metrics.description: Family liaison should assist next of kin with funeral arrangements and coordinate with HR specialists to complete forms and processing for benefits and claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assist with Office of Workers’ Compensation Programs (OWCP), Social Security Administration, Veteran's Administration (if applicable), Public Safety Officers Benefit Program (if applicable), and agency benefit claims; maintain contact over time as community/family support may wane after immediate aftermath.
